1220.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Desktop lacks several operational settings available in Web: Runner scientific environments, execution quotas, Web provider credentials, network proxies, and model token usage. Users have to switch clients to manage the same backend, and separate remote-machine and environment pages obscure which environments belong to which Runner.

Bring these capabilities into Desktop using its existing settings layout, with a clear distinction between deployment-wide configuration and individual Runner details.

### Design Ideas

- Add a unified **Runtime environments** settings entry. The overview lists built-in and remote Runners plus global Conda/Pip download sources. Each Runner detail contains its connection/resources and its own scientific environments, including initialization, creation, package installation and deletion of custom environments.
- Keep system settings deployment-wide. Remove the project-specific Runner allowlist from this surface. Unspecified Runner selection follows the registered catalog, including later registrations; explicit Project/Session selections, including empty lists, retain their restrictions. Do not add a session Runner picker in this change.
- Add **Run quotas** for subagent concurrency, retained execution output, workspace size and upload limits. Saving an upload quota updates Desktop upload preflight immediately.
- Add **Web search** settings for JiuwenSwarm. Group DeepSeek with the other paid search providers, share its saved key with the webpage-fetch selector, and explain the charge when DeepSeek fetching is selected. Avoid separate DeepSeek enable switches.
- Add **Network proxies** for the global default, proxy registry, bypass list, connectivity testing and MCP overrides. Keep bypass editing inside the global-default section. Do not imply that these policies control JiuwenSwarm's native Web tools.
- Add **Model usage** beside Models: Today / Last 7 days / Last 30 days / All time, three token totals, a flat per-model table, refresh and update time. Distinguish unreported fields from reported zeros. Omit cost estimates, charts, project/session trees and export controls from the initial Desktop view.

Reuse Desktop typography, grouped rows, switches, dialogs and responsive spacing. Keep the settings visible rather than behind additional advanced-section disclosures.

### Involved Public APIs

Reuse the existing Runner environment, environment-source, quota, Web settings, proxy and usage analytics routes.

Add optional per-field reporting coverage to analytics totals and daily model rows so clients can distinguish missing usage from zero usage. Allow token-only analytics requests to omit exchange rates with `includeExchangeRates=false`; existing clients retain their current response behavior.

Runner defaults use the current registry when no selection was specified. Explicit unified selections and legacy API writes remain supported, including local-only legacy empty selections and explicit empty unified selections that disable execution.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- Desktop settings, localization and upload preflight.
- Shared analytics/Runner-selection schema and API persistence/selection resolution.
- Runner-owned environment management and remote workspace discovery.
- JiuwenSwarm Web-settings synchronization and provider credentials.
- Existing Web clients, whose settings and analytics UI remain available.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Use focused component, formatting and backend tests to cover:

- Runner overview/detail navigation, ownership of multiple environments, disconnected states, initialization errors, creation, package installation, deletion and global package-source writes.
- Quota boundaries and upload-preflight updates; credential keep/replace/remove behavior; proxy inheritance, bypass editing, connectivity results and referenced-proxy deletion failures.
- Default Runner availability after later registration and reload, explicit-selection precedence, empty selections, unusable Runner admission and malformed input.
- Usage date ranges and time zones, per-profile aggregation, cache-token non-duplication, reported zeros versus missing fields, delayed-response isolation, retry and refresh failures.
- Desktop/API type checks and Desktop production build.

Before marking the implementation ready for review, inspect the rendered settings at normal and narrow widths and verify the relevant JiuwenSwarm-backed flows against a running stack.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The requested resource settings can be managed in Desktop without opening Web.
- [ ] Runner details clearly contain that Runner's environments; global package sources remain in the overview.
- [ ] System settings do not show project-specific Runner selection controls.
- [ ] Unspecified selection includes registered Runners dynamically; existing explicit restrictions and execution admission remain enforced.
- [ ] Credentials remain write-only; failed changes are visible and do not appear saved.
- [ ] The token page is deployment-wide, compact, date-filterable and honest about unreported usage.
- [ ] Focused regression tests, affected-package type checks and the Desktop production build pass.

Commands include:

```sh
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/api typecheck
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build
pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop exec tsx --import ./tests/support/css-preload.mjs --test tests/migrated-settings.test.tsx tests/model-usage-settings.test.tsx tests/settings-pages.test.tsx tests/settings-screens.test.tsx
pnpm exec tsx --test packages/schema/src/project-runner-selection.test.ts services/api/src/runner-defaults.test.ts services/api/src/runner-management.test.ts services/api/src/model-usage.test.ts services/api/src/configuration/runner-adapter.integration.test.ts
```

### Additional Information

This proposal focuses on Desktop parity with a simpler presentation. It does not add session-level Runner selection, a new execution scheduler, model billing, or a replacement Web interface.

1223.body:
## 背景

积分规则已确定：首次登录赠送 500 积分，每个自然日首次登录自动发放 100 积分，累计签到每满 7 天再发放 50 积分，且不设发放上限。

当前产品尚未提供任何账户相关页面与管理入口：用户无法确认今日奖励是否到账、看不到积分花在哪里，也没有自助管理登录设备的入口；运营与客服在核对流水、发放补偿、处理账号风险时只能直连数据库，既不安全也不可审计。

本 issue 包含两份需求文档：面向用户的账户中心（在本仓验收）、面向运营的用户管理后台（不在本仓验收）。

---

## 一、ScienceDiscovery 用户账户中心（用户信息详情页）需求文档

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 文档版本 | v1.1 |
| 状态 | 待评审 |
| 更新日期 | 2026-11-18 |

在应用内提供可自助查看的账户页：用户能确认积分余额与 token 折算、今日奖励到账与满 7 天进度、积分消耗去向，并管理登录设备与昵称。

### 01 需求详情

#### 背景与问题

积分规则已经确定：首次登录赠送 500 积分，每个自然日首次登录自动发放 100 积分，累计签到每满 7 天再发放 50 积分，且不设发放上限。当前产品尚未提供账户相关页面，用户无法确认今日奖励是否到账、看不到积分花在哪里，也没有自助管理登录设备的入口。为此新增用户信息详情页：点击用户按钮后打开抽屉，让用户在一屏内看清余额、今日奖励与消耗去向，并能管理登录设备与昵称。

### 02 需求设计方案

#### 页面形态与信息架构

新增用户详情入口，点击后以抽屉形式展示账户信息，具体位置、尺寸与关闭方式按现有设计规范确定。抽屉内自上而下分为四层：

1. **账户概览**：昵称与加入天数 → 可用积分 → token 折算与可对话轮数 → 累计获得 / 累计消耗 / 今日到账。
2. **今日奖励**：今日到账状态与 +100 积分 → 7 天进度（第 1–7 天）→ 距离满 7 天还差几天 → “每天自动发放、不设上限”的说明。
3. **明细 / 用量 / 设备 / 设置**：四个标签页，默认停在“明细”。
4. **页脚**：1 积分折算提示与“退出登录”。

页面只展示积分与 token，不出现任何金额；每日奖励为登录自动到账，不设签到按钮。

### 03 需求规格

#### 功能需求清单

| 编号 | 功能 | 规则与结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | 账户概览 | 展示头像首字母、昵称、加入天数、可用积分；token 折算 = 积分 × 4 万，按“万”取整；展示可对话轮数（每轮按 2 积分估算）、累计获得、累计消耗、今日到账。**不展示任何金额。** |
| FR-02 | 今日奖励与 7 天进度 | 当日已发放时显示“今日登录奖励已到账 +100 积分”，未发放时显示“登录后自动到账”；7 个格子按顺序展示到账积分（第 1 天 600、第 2–6 天各 100、第 7 天 +50），当天高亮；提示“再连续 N 天可获满 7 天奖励 +50 积分”。 |
| FR-03 | 积分流水与消耗明细 | 按时间倒序展示最近 10–20 条流水，含类型、时间、变动积分、变动后余额；支持“全部 / 获得 / 消耗”筛选；点击模型调用记录可展开模型、输入 / 缓存 / 输出 token、耗时与 token 合计。 |
| FR-04 | 用量统计 | 展示近 5 天调用次数、消耗积分、token 合计；柱状图按日展示消耗积分；底部展示平均每次消耗积分与最常用模型。统计口径与流水一致。 |
| FR-05 | 登录设备管理 | 展示设备名称、平台、最近活跃时间；当前设备带“当前”标记且不可退出；其他设备可“退出”，点击后该会话立即失效并从列表移除，提示“已退出该设备”。不展示 IP、内部设备 ID 与完整 openid。 |
| FR-06 | 昵称与退出登录 | 昵称可编辑（1–24 字符），保存后抽屉头部与用户按钮同步更新；邮箱只读；页脚“退出登录”清除本机会话并跳转登录页。积分规则以折叠说明提供。 |

### 04 需求验收标准

| 编号 | 对应功能 | 验收条件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | 账户概览 | 可用积分与账户实际余额一致；token 折算 = 积分 × 4 万，误差不超过 1 万；累计获得、累计消耗、今日到账满足“获得 − 消耗 = 余额”；全页不出现 ¥、元、价格、成本等金额表述。 |
| AC-02 | 今日奖励与 7 天进度 | 当日已发放时显示“已到账 +100 积分”，未发放时显示“登录后自动到账”；页面不存在签到按钮；第 1 天显示 600、第 2–6 天显示 100、第 7 天显示 +50；当天高亮，“再连续 N 天”与实际剩余天数一致。 |
| AC-03 | 积分流水与消耗明细 | 记录按时间倒序，相邻记录满足“上一条余额 + 本条变动 = 本条余额”；“获得 / 消耗”筛选结果正确；消耗行展开后展示模型、输入/缓存/输出 token、耗时与 token 合计，获得行不可展开。 |
| AC-04 | 用量统计 | 近 5 天消耗积分之和与流水中的消耗合计一致；调用次数与实际记录数一致；今天无消耗时柱状图显示灰色占位。 |
| AC-05 | 登录设备管理 | 当前设备带“当前”标记且无退出按钮；点击其他设备“退出”后立即从列表移除并提示；被退出设备下一次请求被拒绝并要求重新登录。 |
| AC-06 | 昵称与退出登录 | 昵称保存后抽屉头部与用户按钮同步更新，刷新后保持；空值或超过 24 字符时无法保存并有提示；邮箱不可编辑；退出登录后回到登录页，本地不残留会话与用户数据。 |

---

## 二、ScienceDiscovery 用户管理后台需求文档（本需求不在 ScienceDiscovery 代码仓验收）

| 项目 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 文档版本 | v1.0 |
| 状态 | 待评审 |
| 更新日期 | 2026-11-18 |

为运营与客服提供后台：能检索任意用户、查看其积分与用量全貌，并在必要时调整积分、限制账号或强制下线，所有操作留痕可追溯。

### 01 需求详情

#### 背景与问题

前台账户中心解决了用户“看得到”的问题，但运营与客服还需要“查得到、管得住”：用户反馈积分异常时，需要核对其流水与用量；出现滥用或账号风险时，需要限制账号或强制下线；活动补偿需要人工发放积分。当前缺少统一的管理入口，上述动作只能依赖数据库直连，既不可审计也存在误操作风险。为此新增用户管理后台：以用户列表为入口，进入单个用户后可查看账户、流水、用量与会话，并执行受权限约束、必须填写原因的管理操作。

### 02 需求设计方案

#### 页面形态与信息架构

后台为独立站点，与前台账户体系分离，通过账号密码完成登录，仅授权账号可进入。页面由列表页与详情页两级构成：

1. **概览与用户列表**：顶部展示总用户数、今日新增、今日活跃、今日消耗积分、在线会话、冻结用户；列表支持按昵称或标识搜索，按状态、在线状态筛选，按余额、消耗、最近活跃排序，并分页展示。
2. **用户详情**：上半部分为身份与积分概览，下半部分为流水、用量、会话、操作审计四个区块。
3. **管理操作**：积分调整、账号状态修改、强制下线，均在详情页内发起，需二次确认并填写原因。
4. **操作留痕**：每次写操作记录操作人、对象、动作、原因、时间与来源地址，可在用户审计与全局审计中查询。

管理操作与只读查看在权限上分离，只读账号不可执行任何写操作。

### 03 需求规格

#### 功能需求清单

| 编号 | 功能 | 规则与结果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | 登录与权限 | 账号密码校验通过后建立后台会话；连续输错达到阈值临时锁定；禁用账号拒绝登录；会话超时自动失效；写操作仅对具备操作权限的账号开放。 |
| FR-02 | 概览与用户列表 | 概览展示总用户、今日新增、今日活跃、今日消耗积分、在线会话、冻结用户；列表展示昵称、用户标识、状态、余额、累计消耗、最近活跃与是否在线；支持关键词搜索、状态与在线筛选、三种排序与分页。 |
| FR-03 | 用户详情概览 | 展示昵称、用户标识与脱敏外部账号、注册时间、账号状态、邮箱、最近登录、积分更新时间；并以卡片展示可用余额、累计消耗、累计获得、在线会话数，冻结积分单独标注。 |
| FR-04 | 流水、用量与审计 | 流水按时间倒序分页展示类型、变动积分、变动后余额、备注与时间；用量按日展示请求数、消耗积分与 token 量，默认近 30 天；审计展示该用户的全部管理操作记录。 |

### 1. User Account Center (User Profile Details Page) Requirements Document

| --- | --- |
| Version | v1.1 |
| Status | Pending review |
| Last updated | 2026-11-18 |

Provide a self-service account page inside the product: users can confirm their credit balance and its token equivalent, verify today's reward and 7-day progress, see where credits were spent, and manage signed-in devices and their nickname.

#### 01 Requirement Details

**Background and Problem.** The credit rules are already fixed: 500 credits on first sign-in, 100 credits granted automatically on the first sign-in of each calendar day, an extra 50 credits for every cumulative 7 days of check-ins, with no cap on issuance. The product currently provides no account-related page, so users cannot confirm whether today's reward has arrived, cannot see where their credits went, and have no self-service entry point for managing signed-in devices. This requirement therefore adds a user profile details page: clicking the user button opens a drawer where users can see their balance, today's reward and spending in one screen, and manage signed-in devices and their nickname.

#### 02 Solution Design

**Page Form and Information Architecture.** Add a user details entry point; clicking it opens a drawer that displays account information. The exact position, size and dismissal behavior follow the existing design system. The drawer is organized top to bottom into four layers:

1. **Account overview**: nickname and days since joining → available credits → token equivalent and estimated conversation turns → total earned / total spent / earned today.
2. **Today's reward**: today's crediting status and +100 credits → 7-day progress (days 1–7) → days remaining until the 7-day reward → the note "granted automatically every day, no cap".
3. **Ledger / Usage / Devices / Settings**: four tabs, defaulting to "Ledger".
4. **Footer**: the credit-to-token note and "Sign out".

The page shows credits and tokens only, never any monetary amount. Daily rewards are granted automatically on sign-in; there is no check-in button.

| ID | Feature | Rules and Results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | Account overview | Show the avatar initial, nickname, days since joining and available credits; token equivalent = credits × 40,000, rounded to the nearest ten thousand; show estimated conversation turns (2 credits per turn), total earned, total spent and earned today. **No monetary amounts are displayed.** |
| FR-02 | Today's reward and 7-day progress | When granted today, show "Today's sign-in reward received: +100 credits"; otherwise show "Granted automatically after sign-in". The seven cells show the credits granted in order (day 1: 600, days 2–6: 100 each, day 7: +50), with today highlighted; show "N more consecutive days for the 7-day reward: +50 credits". |
| FR-03 | Credit ledger and usage details | Show the latest 10–20 entries in reverse chronological order with type, time, credit change and balance after the change; support All / Earned / Spent filters; clicking a model-call entry expands the model, input / cached / output tokens, duration and total tokens. |
| FR-04 | Usage statistics | Show calls, credits spent and total tokens for the last 5 days; a bar chart of credits spent per day; average credits per call and the most used model at the bottom. The scope matches the ledger. |

### 2. User Management Console Requirements Document (Acceptance is out of scope for the ScienceDiscovery code repository)

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Version | v1.0 |
| Status | Pending review |
| Last updated | 2026-11-18 |

Provide operations and support teams with a console: search any user, review their credits and usage in full, and when necessary adjust credits, restrict accounts or force sign-out, with every action traceable.

#### 01 Requirement Details

**Background and Problem.** The user-facing account center solves "can users see it", but operations and support also need "can we find it and control it": when a user reports a credit anomaly, their ledger and usage must be checked; when abuse or account risk appears, the account must be restricted or sessions terminated; campaign compensation requires manual credit grants. There is currently no unified management entry point, so these actions can only be performed through direct database access, which is neither auditable nor safe from mistakes. This requirement therefore adds a user management console: starting from a user list, staff can open an individual user to review the account, ledger, usage and sessions, and perform permission-controlled management actions that require a reason.

#### 02 Solution Design

**Page Form and Information Architecture.** The console is a standalone site, separate from the user-facing account system, signed in with a username and password and accessible only to authorized accounts. It consists of two levels, a list page and a details page:

1. **Overview and user list**: the top shows total users, new users today, active users today, credits spent today, online sessions and frozen users; the list supports search by nickname or identifier, filtering by status and online state, sorting by balance, spending or last active, and pagination.
2. **User details**: the upper part shows identity and credit overview; the lower part contains four blocks — ledger, usage, sessions and operation audit.
3. **Management actions**: credit adjustments, account status changes and forced sign-out, all initiated from the details page with confirmation and a required reason.
4. **Traceability**: every write action records the operator, target, action, reason, time and source address, and can be queried in the user audit and the global audit.

Management actions and read-only viewing are separated by permission; read-only accounts cannot perform any write action.

#### 03 Requirement Specification

| ID | Feature | Rules and Results |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-01 | Sign-in and permissions | A backend session is created after the username and password are verified; repeated failures beyond a threshold lock the account temporarily; disabled accounts are refused; sessions expire automatically; write actions are available only to accounts with operation permission. |
| FR-02 | Overview and user list | The overview shows total users, new users today, active users today, credits spent today, online sessions and frozen users; the list shows nickname, user identifier, status, balance, total spent, last active and online state; it supports keyword search, status and online filters, three sort orders and pagination. |
| FR-03 | User details overview | Show nickname, user identifier and masked external account, registration time, account status, email, last sign-in and credit update time; cards show available balance, total spent, total earned and online sessions, with frozen credits called out separately. |
| FR-04 | Ledger, usage and audit | The ledger shows type, credit change, balance after the change, remark and time in reverse chronological order with pagination; usage shows requests, credits spent and tokens per day for the last 30 days by default; the audit shows all management actions on that user. |
| FR-05 | Credit adjustment | Credits can be adjusted up or down, within a per-action system limit, with a required reason of limited length; the resulting balance may not be negative; on success an admin-type ledger entry is created immediately and an audit record is written, and the latest balance is returned. |
| FR-06 | Status and forced sign-out | Account status can be switched among normal, restricted, frozen and similar states, with the change written to the audit; the session list shows device, platform, state and last active, and a selected session can be forced offline, taking effect immediately and recording both an audit entry and a sign-in event. |

#### 04 Acceptance Criteria

| ID | Feature | Acceptance criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AC-01 | Sign-in and permissions | A wrong password cannot sign in, and repeated failures beyond the threshold lock the account temporarily; disabled accounts cannot sign in; read-only accounts see no write entry points, and calling write APIs directly returns a permission error. |
| AC-02 | Overview and user list | The six overview metrics match database statistics; keyword search matches nickname and user identifier; status and online filters return correct results; all three sort orders work; after paging, the total and page number are consistent, and an empty result shows a clear message. |
| AC-03 | User details overview | Identity information on the details page matches the list and the database; the balance matches the balance of the latest ledger entry; total spent and total earned satisfy "earned − spent = balance"; the external account is shown only in masked form. |
| AC-04 | Ledger, usage and audit | The ledger is in reverse chronological order and further pages can be loaded; usage dates are continuous with no duplicates and the totals match spending in the period; the audit list is in reverse chronological order and contains only that user's records. |
| AC-05 | Credit adjustment | Submission is blocked when the reason is missing or too long; exceeding the per-action limit is rejected; an adjustment that would make the balance negative is rejected; after success the balance, ledger and audit are consistent, and the ledger remark equals the entered reason. |
| AC-06 | Status and forced sign-out | Status changes take effect immediately in both the list and the details page, and subsequent requests from a restricted account are rejected per the rules; after a forced sign-out the target session is invalidated immediately and the user must sign in again; both actions record the operator, target, time and source address in the audit. |

1229.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

On a Chinese Windows host, an Idea Tree research can be created and read back one at a time, but **listing** the session's researches fails with a GBK decode error, so the desktop Idea Tree card never renders. The asymmetry is a decoding bug, not a missing record.

Observed in a real journey (measured by PR-bot-2号 while validating #1169 on this machine): `/idea-tree` handed off successfully and created `research-5e8c3f04…`; a `get` for that research returned a healthy state — `status: running`, `phase: aggregate`, `round: 1`, `268290` tokens, 13 nodes and 12 edges. The very next list call returned an error instead:

```
GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research
{"error":"'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position …"}
```

`get` works, `list` fails, for the same research.

**Why the two disagree — verified in the code on main `eb5f66e8`:**

| Path | Code | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Write | `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:106` opens the checkpoint with `encoding='utf-8'`, and `:109` dumps with `ensure_ascii=False` | state files legitimately contain raw non-ASCII bytes |
| Single read | `research.py:129` — `json.loads(self.path(...).read_text())` — **no `encoding=`** | `Path.read_text()` falls back to the locale default (cp936/GBK on a Chinese Windows host) |
| List read | `research.py:133` — `json.loads(p.read_text())` for every `*.json` in the directory — **no `encoding=`** | same locale-default decode |
| `get` dispatch | `research_service.py:88-95` `state_for()`: a research that is `_running` returns the **in-memory** state; only a non-running one falls back to `store().read()` | a running research's `get` never decodes the file, so it succeeds |
| `list` dispatch | `research_service.py:148-149` always calls `store().list(...)` | always decodes every file on disk |

So the failure is exactly where the report put it: the Python side decodes a UTF-8 checkpoint with the platform default encoding. `0x80` is a UTF-8 continuation byte, which GBK cannot decode — the error names the codec the interpreter chose, not anything the file did wrong.

**This also predicts a second failure the report did not reach:** once a research is no longer in memory (paused, completed, or after the service restarts), `get` takes the `store().read()` branch and will fail the same way — i.e. every non-ASCII research becomes unreadable after a restart, not just unlistable.

Minimal reproduction (Chinese Windows, non-UTF-8 default encoding):

1. Start the stack on a host whose `locale.getpreferredencoding()` is `cp936` (a default Chinese Windows install; no `PYTHONUTF8=1`).
2. Create a research through `/idea-tree <objective>` where the objective or a node hypothesis contains non-ASCII text (Chinese is enough), and let it reach `running`.
3. `GET /api/sessions/{projectId}/idea-tree/research/{researchId}` (via `POST {"operation":"get","researchId":…}`) → returns the state.
4. `GET /api/sessions/{sessionId}/idea-tree/research` → `{"error":"'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position …"}`.

Impact: the desktop Idea Tree card renders nothing at all (the list is what it reads), while the research keeps running and spending tokens; the same decode path breaks `get` for any research that is not currently in memory. This is a blocker for #1169 (desktop Idea Tree adaptation).

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Chinese Windows 11 (system locale cp936 / GBK; `PYTHONUTF8` not set) |
| Python | 3.12 (the evolve service's own venv) — `Path.read_text()` defaults to the locale encoding here |
| Engine | Idea Tree Python research loop inside the evolve service (`services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/`) |
| State location | `$SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_DIR/idea-research/<projectId>/<sessionId>/<researchId>.json` (UTF-8, `ensure_ascii=False`) |
| Client | Desktop 0.4.0 (Idea Tree card), API route `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (`/idea-tree/research`) |
| Observed research | `research-5e8c3f04…`, status `running`, phase `aggregate`, round 1, 268 290 tokens, 13 nodes / 12 edges |
| Failing call | `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` |

## Additional Information

Suggested fix (small, local to the engine):

- Pass `encoding='utf-8'` explicitly in `research.py:129` and `research.py:133`, and sweep the rest of `vendor/idea_tree` for `read_text()` / `open()` without an encoding (`idea_tree_service.py:33` writes through a file object and `:49` reads with `read_text()` — same class of defect for the legacy tree store).
- A regression test that does not depend on the host locale: write a checkpoint containing non-ASCII text through the UTF-8 writer, then force the default encoding (for example `monkeypatch.setattr(locale, "getpreferredencoding", lambda **_kw: "cp936")`, or run the helper with `PYTHONUTF8=0` and a `cp936` locale) and assert that both `read()` and `list()` return the non-ASCII content intact.
- Optional hardening: fail loudly in one place (a single `load_state(path)` helper used by both readers) instead of two ad-hoc `read_text()` calls.

The measurement above (research id, counters, error text) comes from PR-bot-2号's real run on this host; the code pointers and the `get`/`list` dispatch explanation were verified against `main` `eb5f66e8` before filing.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e` ("fix(mac-release): only the updater-contract blockmap name passes 5f") |
| Desktop shell | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 (`application/package.json`) |
| Engine files | `services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py:106,129,133`; `research_service.py:88-95,148-149` |
| Python | 3.12 (evolve service venv) |

1232.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version (confirmed by inspecting current upstream main).
- [x] I have included the available environment information and a minimal reproduction scenario below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

A model rate-limit error interrupted an Idea Tree research task during use on November 18, 2026. A temporary provider limit should allow the current model request to resume after a delay, without requiring the user to manually continue the research.

**Actual behavior:** HTTP 429 is not retried by the Idea Tree research transport. It raises an exception immediately, and the research engine records the task as `interrupted`.

**Expected behavior:** Retry transient HTTP 429 responses with bounded backoff, honoring the provider's retry delay when available. Keep completed research stages and the current task alive while waiting. The wait must respect pause/cancel and execution budgets. If the retry budget is exhausted or the error represents a permanent quota/configuration problem, report a clear interruption reason.

**Minimal reproduction scenario (deterministic fault injection):**

1. Start an Idea Tree research task with a configured model.
2. Make the model endpoint return HTTP 429 for one stage request, then return a valid successful completion on the next request. For example, use this first response:

   ```http
   HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
   Content-Type: application/json
   Retry-After: 1

   {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Too many requests; retry shortly"}}
   ```

3. Observe that the research becomes `interrupted` on the first response, rather than waiting and issuing the next request.

This response is a proposed reproduction fixture, not a captured production response. The original provider error body and full traceback are unavailable; the user reported a model rate-limit failure. The deterministic scenario was established by code inspection and has not been executed in this report.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Affected component: Idea Tree research service in the Python Evolve sidecar, using the API's internal Evolve LLM proxy.
- Call path: `createIdeaResearchClient` → `/internal/evolve-llm/:researchId/v1/chat/completions` → `handleEvolveCompletion` → `completeChatRequest(..., streamUpstream=true)`; retry ownership remains with the Python research transport.
- The original deployment version, model/provider, client, OS, and runtime versions were not captured. The control flow described here is present in the upstream source revision below.

### Additional Information

The retry gap is specific to this call path:

- [Idea Tree transport](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py#L179-L201) makes at most two attempts, but only retries `error.code >= 500`, immediately. A 429 goes directly to `RuntimeError`.
- [Research engine exception handling](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e/services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/vendor/idea_tree/research.py#L569-L578) changes the research status to `interrupted` for an unhandled failure.
- [The shared completion adapter](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e/packages/model/src/completion.ts#L79-L88) explicitly sets `maxRetries: 0` for this path because the sidecar owns retry and budget decisions. Increasing `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES` therefore does not fix Idea Tree research.
- The ordinary Agent model client already retries HTTP 429 and 5xx by default, which makes the research service's behavior inconsistent.

Suggested regression coverage: a transient 429 followed by success continues the same research stage; repeated 429s terminate after a bounded budget; completed stages are preserved; pause/cancel interrupts a backoff wait. Retry delay metadata must reach whichever layer owns the retry.

### Version Information

- Latest upstream main inspected: `eb5f66e80ac7308bb49a1842737d8bafb3bd2a4e` (fetched on November 18, 2026).
- The affected transport and completion code also match the local revision where this behavior was investigated.

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The environment and the exact run are named below, so this is reproducible from the job log alone.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The `UT` job reports **success** while executing **no Python test at all**. A failing Python case therefore cannot turn the gate red — the suites exist, are tagged, and are silently never run.

### What was observed

On PR #1231 (head `49354a23ca6a262bc79a6022c38dc675798143ba`), job **`UT`** = `134700142074` in run `44274693462` finished `success`. Its executed plan contains 681 entries:

| extension | count |
| --- | --- |
| `.ts` | 474 |
| `.tsx` | 159 |
| `.mjs` | 43 |
| none | 5 |
| **`.py`** | **0** |

Two independent greps over the same job log:

```
services/evolve/tests   -> 0 occurrences
.py::                   -> 0 occurrences
```

The environment for Python *was* prepared in that same job, so this is not a skipped setup:

```
2026-11-18T09:20:34.3171967Z Prepare: uv sync --project services/evolve --locked --extra test --extra candidates
2026-11-18T09:20:35.6487682Z Prepare: uv pip install --python .../services/evolve/.venv/bin/python coverage>=7.6,<8
```

### What the runner is supposed to collect

`test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs:112-113`:

```js
export const pythonProjects = Object.freeze(['paper', 'gateway', 'memory-graph', 'evolve', 'adapter']);
export const pythonSources = project => `services/${project}/tests/test_*.py`;
```

`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs:257-261`:

```js
if(needUT)for(const project of pythonProjects){
  const dir=join(outputDir,`collect-${project}`);mkdirSync(dir,{recursive:true});
  const sources=[...globSync(pythonSources(project),{cwd:root})].sort();
  catalog.push(...collect({root,files:sources,outputDir:dir,python:python(project),pytestPlugins:pythonPlugins[project]??[],env:projectEnv(env,project)}));
}
```

So for `evolve` the scope is `services/evolve/tests/test_*.py` — 20+ files exist there — and that loop runs under the same `needUT` that produced the `uv sync` above.

### Why it matters

Every Python suite under `services/*/tests` is currently unguarded on PRs. This is not theoretical: PR #1231 adds two regression cases for a UTF-8 decode bug, both tagged `category:ut`, and neither is executed by the job that is supposed to gate them. Any existing Python test could regress without any PR check noticing.

Note that the same plan shows no `.py` for **any** of the five `pythonProjects`, not only `evolve`.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

`Nightly` (`.github/workflows/nightly.yml`) is the L4 `daily` gate on `main`. It is triggered by a 16:00 UTC cron (`- cron: "0 16 * * *"`, line 33) and by `workflow_dispatch` (line 34). Its own header already says GitHub "drops or delays runs when its queue is busy — treat a missing night as a scheduling miss and re-dispatch rather than as a build failure".

GitHub is now consistently creating the scheduled run hours late. The ten most recent `event=schedule` runs returned by the Actions API are:

| Scheduled 16:00 UTC | Run created (UTC) | Lateness | Run |

| 2026-11-11 | 2026-11-11T22:35:07Z | 6 h 35 m | [43112992255](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/43112992255) |

| 2026-11-08 | 2026-11-08T20:20:32Z | 4 h 20 m | [42519625781](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42519625781) |

The times above are the run's `created_at` from the API, i.e. when GitHub created the run, not when a step started. Every one was created between **4 h 20 m and 8 h 07 m after the 16:00 UTC occurrence** it belongs to. The run before these ten, [42409367796](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/42409367796), was created at 2026-11-07T20:05:46Z and was 4 h 05 m late, so this is not a single bad night.

16:00 UTC is 00:00 in Asia/Shanghai, and the workflow header intends the run to start overnight and "finish by the working morning". A run created at 04:20–08:07 Asia/Shanghai has not done that, and its long real-model suite runs after that creation time.

There is also a same-day dispatch on 2026-11-18: [run 44361037291](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291) was created at 2026-11-18T17:39:13Z as a `workflow_dispatch` by `agent-ci-infra-bot`. At the time of the API read (2026-11-18T19:37Z) there was still no `event=schedule` run for that day's 16:00 UTC occurrence. The API does not record why the dispatch was started; it is consistent with the re-dispatch the workflow header describes.

The result is that the normal 16:00 UTC start depends on GitHub's cron queue, and the workaround is a manual or one-off bot re-dispatch. The plan below makes the normal start independent of that queue and keeps the cron only as a guarded fallback.

## Design Ideas

Both parts below are one plan, not alternatives. Part 1 moves the normal start out of GitHub's cron queue. Part 2 makes the cron safe when it does arrive, so it cannot cancel a running dispatch run or create a duplicate after a successful one.

### Part 1 — start the run from the bot schedule

In the bot console, ask the management assistant, or add a project scheduled task on the project's `定时任务与通知` page. Schedule it shortly after 16:00 UTC (for example 16:05 UTC, or 00:05 Asia/Shanghai if the page uses local time) with this instruction:

> start nightly.yml on main; first check that no run of it is queued or in progress, and if one is, start nothing

That gives the project a primary start that is not GitHub's cron queue, and the check keeps it from adding a run when a person or the fallback has already started one. Keep `workflow_dispatch` so the same task, or a person, can still start the workflow.

### Part 2 — change the workflow

Keep `workflow_dispatch`. Keep `schedule` with `- cron: "0 16 * * *"` only as a fallback. Add a workflow-level `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a scheduled run waits for a running dispatch run instead of cancelling it. Add a first `guard` job that, on `schedule` only, checks whether a `workflow_dispatch` run of `nightly.yml` succeeded since the most recent 16:00 UTC; if one did, it sets `run=false` and every other job is skipped. On `workflow_dispatch` it always sets `run=true`.

This is the concrete adaptation for the existing `stamp`, `gate` and `report` jobs:

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 16 * * *"   # fallback only; the bot schedule starts the run
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # A scheduled run queues behind a running dispatch run instead of cancelling it.
  group: nightly-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Check for a successful dispatch run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      actions: read        # gh run list
      contents: read
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          run=true
          if [[ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" == "schedule" ]]; then
            # The most recent scheduled time: 16:00 UTC today, or yesterday
            # when a delayed run is created before 16:00 UTC.
            since=$(date -u -d '16:00 today' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
            if (( $(date -u +%s) < $(date -u -d "$since" +%s) )); then
              since=$(date -u -d '16:00 yesterday' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
            fi
            count=$(gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" -w nightly.yml \
              -e workflow_dispatch -s success --created ">=$since" \
              --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq 'length')
            if (( count > 0 )); then
              run=false
            fi
          fi
          echo "run=$run" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  stamp:
    name: Stamp the build
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.stamp.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - id: stamp
        run: |
          date=$(TZ=Asia/Shanghai date +%Y%m%d)
          echo "version=nightly-${date}-${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  gate:
    name: Gate
    needs: [guard, stamp]
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      profile: daily
      release-version: ${{ needs.stamp.outputs.version }}

  report:
    name: Report the outcome
    needs: [guard, stamp, gate]
    if: always() && needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    # ... the existing report steps are unchanged ...
```

The guard job declares `actions: read`; the workflow-level `contents: read` stays. It uses the workflow's own `github.token`, not a new secret. The `--created ">=$since"` filter and `-s success` mean only a successful dispatch created at or after the scheduled time suppresses the fallback; a failed or cancelled dispatch does not. `gh run list --limit 1` is enough because only the existence of a match matters. If the `gh run list` call itself fails, the guard job fails and the workflow is red; it does not silently guess that no dispatch exists.

GitHub keeps at most one pending run per concurrency group. With one bot start and one cron fallback that is enough: the fallback waits for the running dispatch, and after the dispatch succeeds the guard skips the duplicate. A third run arriving while one is running and one is already pending could replace the older pending one; that is GitHub's queue behaviour and is not changed by `cancel-in-progress: false`.

## Involved Public APIs

No product API, UI, CLI or schema changes. The change is limited to `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` and the project-level bot schedule.

The guard job declares `actions: read` so `gh run list` can read workflow runs; the workflow-level `contents: read` remains. No new repository secret or credential is needed: `github.token` is the existing per-run token. The bot scheduled task uses the existing `workflow_dispatch` entry point. The cron trigger stays in place.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- **L4 `daily` gate:** `stamp` produces the `nightly-YYYYMMDD-<sha>` version, `gate` calls the reusable `ci.yml` with `profile: daily`, and `report` writes the outcome. Their bodies and inputs do not change; only the guard condition is added.
- **Release:** `release.yml` is a separate workflow and is not affected by this plan.
- **Product code and tests:** no product path changes. The real-model journeys, case selection and evaluation are untouched.
- **Project automation:** the bot console / `定时任务与通知` task is project automation, not repository code; it needs no repository change from this Issue.

## Test Design and Test Plan

This Issue recommends a change; it does not implement it. The repository's implementation should verify the following, none of which requires a paid real-model run:

- `actionlint` (or at least a YAML parse) passes on the updated `nightly.yml`.
- A `workflow_dispatch` run still executes `stamp`, `gate` and `report`; the guard sets `run=true` for that event.
- A scheduled run with no successful dispatch created since 16:00 UTC sets `run=true` and executes the three jobs normally.
- A scheduled run with a successful dispatch created since 16:00 UTC sets `run=false`; `stamp`, `gate` and `report` are skipped, and the run's conclusion is success rather than a red `report` failure.
- A failed or cancelled dispatch does not suppress the scheduled run, because only `-s success` matches.
- With a dispatch run in progress, a scheduled run queues in the same concurrency group and does not cancel the dispatch; after the dispatch succeeds, the scheduled run's guard skips the duplicate.
- The project scheduled task starts exactly one run when none is queued or in progress, and starts nothing when one is.
- If the repository adds a workflow-contract test, assert the guard's `-e workflow_dispatch -s success` filter and the `needs`/`if` values on `stamp`, `gate` and `report`. The repository already has tests that read `nightly.yml` (for example `.ci/case-execution.test.mjs`), so there is an existing place for such a contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The bot console or a project scheduled task on `定时任务与通知` starts `nightly.yml` on `main` shortly after 16:00 UTC, after checking that no run of it is queued or in progress; if one is, it starts nothing.
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` remains available and starts the full workflow.
- [ ] The 16:00 UTC cron remains as a fallback, and the guard skips the scheduled run when a successful `workflow_dispatch` run was created since the most recent 16:00 UTC.
- [ ] The workflow has `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, so a scheduled run does not cancel a running dispatch run.
- [ ] `stamp`, `gate` and `report` keep their current behaviour on the normal path; the guard only adds the skip condition.
- [ ] The workflow change is reviewed and merged through the repository's normal process, not through this task.

## Additional Information

### Prior recommendation search

I searched open and closed Issues in this repository before writing this. The query terms and results were:

- `nightly.yml` — 17 results; the closest are #1160 (a Nightly failure report) and #850 (a per-case execution table). Neither recommends scheduling.
- `workflow_dispatch` — 18 results; the closest are #615 (a manual-validation workflow) and #243 (a merged PR that removed a release-branch dispatch). Neither is about the late Nightly.
- `in:title schedule Nightly` — only #243, the same merged PR.
- `in:title schedule` — #1029 (an unrelated queued-run retry bug) and #243.
- `nightly delayed` — #1035 (export preview OOM) and #283 (L1–L5 test coverage); neither is about the cron delay.
- `in:title delayed`, `in:title late`, `in:title cron`, `cron delayed Nightly` — no matching Issue.
- `scheduled run late` — 30 results, but none of the items inspected is a recommendation for this workflow.
- `定时任务` and `"scheduled task" Nightly` — no scheduling recommendation for this workflow.

No earlier recommendation exists, and no maintainer closed a scheduling recommendation as not wanted. This is a new Issue rather than a comment.

### Decision and scope

This Issue is a recommendation only. I have not opened a pull request, pushed a branch, or edited `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`. Whether to adopt Part 2, and its exact implementation, is the repository's own decision; a maintainer or code owner must review and merge it through the normal process.

The workflow file at the time of writing is [`.github/workflows/nightly.yml` on `main`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml). The run data above was read from `GET /repos/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/workflows/nightly.yml/runs?event=schedule` and `...?event=workflow_dispatch`.

## Current behavior

The only planned case in the `research-2` shard, `DRB-59 easy Swarm research integration`, was classified `PROVIDER_FAULT`. The shard reported `planned 1 / executed 1 / passed 0 / failed 0 / provider faults 1` and failed with `- e2e-real: 1 provider fault(s) — an unverified case is not a pass`. The full job log gives the case's own error:

```
Error: Main run must complete with readable, nonempty declared final artifacts; delivery_status=partial; run_status=failed; delivered_artifacts=1; run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The job's `stack.log` identifies the failing request as `model-8f784f89-e866-486a-88b8-9d48d6063774`: HTTP 200, 12,117 SSE records / 3,716,762 bytes over 105.9 s, then `"error":{"classification":"network"}`, with `"attempts":1,"retries":0` and `"hasText":true,"hasToolCalls":true`. The next line is:

```
[jiuwenswarm-agent] run of 670fa97d-b9d0-4410-ad9f-ac0d80e75072 failed: [181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

## Expected behavior

DRB-59 completes its declared final artifacts and the shard reports `passed 1 of 1`. A live provider keeping the response open is a precondition of that journey, not a product assertion.

## Causal chain

The gateway accepted the request (`200`), streamed the answer and tool-call deltas for about 106 s, and the upstream connection was reset while answer text had already been exposed. The model gateway's bounded mid-stream retry is deliberately disabled once answer text is visible: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:517` throws when `state.text` is true, so the turn was not replayed and the run failed with the original transport error. The accounting then correctly recorded `PROVIDER_FAULT` (the status-less transport classification from #1071 / #1076). Under the repository's documented policy a provider fault is not a pass, so the downstream jobs failed:

- **Account for real cases** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075589240) reported `Planned 21; executed 20; passed 19; provider faults 1.` and `- PROVIDER_FAULT: ...DRB-59...`.
- **Gate / merge-gate** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075765132) failed with `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`; `.ci/tier-policy.mjs:52` throws because the daily profile requires the `real-scheduled` job to succeed.
- **Report the outcome** (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44361037291/job/135075939143) failed with `RESULT: failure`; it only asserts that the gate result is `success`.

The other 19 real cases in this run passed, so the endpoint was not globally down; the fault is confined to one model turn.

## What was checked and what it rules out

- The failed-step output of job 135002663117, its `error-context.md`, and the `real-e2e-evidence-research-2` artifact (id `14455408997`). The artifact's `stack.log` is the wire-level evidence quoted above. I read it with `gh run download`; the artifact belongs to this run and commit, but its contents and attempt association are my observation, not independently verified.
- Source at the failed SHA: `const MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 4;` (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts:188`) and the `state.text` guard at `:517`. The zero retries are the documented behaviour, not a missing retry loop.
- Existing Issues: #1071 / #1076 added the status-less transport classification; #898 documented that a reset after answer text starts is not replayed; #1222 recorded the same class for DRB-58 in run 44199315530. This run is a new occurrence of that class, not a new repository defect. It is not the cause reported in #1157-#1160, which describe run 43760882196 and a different failure.

## Uncertainty

The gateway diagnostics preserve only `classification: network`; the provider's own reason for closing the connection (load, edge reset, upstream timeout) is not visible. One reset in one request does not establish how widespread the provider problem was.

## Next verification

Re-run `research-2` (or the Nightly) once when the gateway is healthy and check that DRB-59 completes; a pass would separate the outage from the commit. A rerun was not requested here because the independent J5 provisioning failure in the same run (job 135002663249) is not yet established as external; see the separate report for that job. Its own summary step agrees that the planned case is the only failure: the shared plan reads `- e2e-real: passed 0 of 1 planned`, and the problem list names `FAIL: playwright:test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts::…desktop%20%2Fevolve-design%20reaches%20three%20PUCT%20expansions…`.

The job's evidence artifact `real-e2e-evidence-research-6` (artifact id 14490394792; the upload step recorded the zip digest `8e5c0c81…`) belongs to this run and this commit (`E2E_COMMIT_SHA=59d05aa7…`). In it, `real-standard/e2e-real/test-results/desktop-evolve-srbench-rea-ba575-s-on-an-LLM-SRBench-problem-real/` holds:

- `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` — `"search_status": "succeeded"`, `"expansions": 1`; the single search record is `"status": "succeeded"`, `"bestNodeIndex": 1`, `"finishedAt": "2026-11-19T02:10:53.023Z"`, and its confirmed scorecard carries `"solvedThreshold": 0.999` on a `custom_script` criterion.
- `evolve-events.json` (13 events) — the seed (node 0) scored `baselineScore: 0.194226`; the one expansion (node 1) was `"valid": true`, `"score": 1`; then a log event `"planned 24 expansions, made 1; it stopped because target_reward."` and `{"type": "search_finished", "status": "succeeded", "stopReason": "target_reward", "bestTestScore": 1, "expansionsPlanned": 24, "candidates": 2}`.

The search did not stall, lose workers or hit a token ceiling: its first candidate reached the scorecard's solved threshold (test score 1.0 vs 0.999), and the engine stopped there. This run had `E2E_LLM_THINKING_MODE=enabled`, `E2E_LLM_THINKING_EFFORT=low`, so the per-call token ceiling that #1157 described was not involved; provider faults were 0.

That stop is documented product behavior, not a defect in the search. Since #1073 (closing #948) the PUCT engine passes the scorecard threshold as the framework's target stop:

```python
# services/evolve/src/sciencediscovery_evolve/puct_engine.py:399
            "target_reward": float(spec.scorecard.get("solvedThreshold") or 0.999),
```

and `services/evolve/tests/test_puct_engine.py::test_reaching_the_scorecard_s_solved_threshold_ends_the_run` asserts exactly the event shape this run produced (`stopReason == "target_reward"`, `status == "succeeded"`, fewer expansions than planned).

The smoke, however, hard-codes the count and stops polling on any terminal status, including `succeeded`:

```ts
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:441
          || ["budget_exhausted", "failed", "stopped", "succeeded"].includes(status);
// test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts:449
      expect(expanded.length, `The search must record at least ${target} expansions`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target);
```

So the pass condition is only satisfiable when the model's first candidates do not already reach the scorecard threshold — which is model-luck, not a property of the product.

## Same test bytes passed the night before

The spec and workflows are byte-identical between the previous Nightly head and this one: `git diff b2075e4972a5af90804fdd579ee314bfa502be46 59d05aa70a26801e2e907ca49060329028514608 -- test/ .github/` is empty, and `b2075e49` is the last commit touching the spec. Nightly run 44199315530 (head `b2075e49`, final attempt 3) was green, including `Real E2E (research-6)` and `Account for real cases`. This is not a source regression on this head; the difference is whether the design's first candidate already solves the SRBench problem.

## Not the same cause as the open reports

#1157/#1158/#1159 (run 43760882196) describe a different mechanism: two expansions because 22 candidate calls were cut off at the recorded 16000-token per-call ceiling while still thinking, ending on the expansion cap. #1185 (closed, unknown) recorded 0 expansions. Here the search ended `succeeded` on `target_reward` after one expansion, with a valid candidate that scored 1.0. Those reports remain accurate for their runs; this failure needs its own fix.

## Downstream jobs

One cause explains all four failing jobs:

- `Account for real cases` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958) fails "Reconcile every planned identity" with `Planned 21; executed 21; passed 20; provider faults 0.` / `- research-6: SHARD_FAILED` — the only failed case is this one.
- `merge-gate` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286707014) refuses because the scheduled real layer is red: `Error: CI gate failed: real-scheduled: failure`.
- `Report the outcome` (https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408) runs `[[ "${RESULT}" == "success" ]]` with `RESULT: failure`, so it exits 1. It reports the gate; it does not decide it.

No rerun is requested. A rerun could pass by luck if the model's first candidate falls short of 0.999, but the assertion still contradicts the documented stop, so the same red is expected whenever the design solves the problem on its first candidate.

## Expected behavior

A search that reaches the scorecard's `solvedThreshold` on its first expansion must end `succeeded` with `stopReason: "target_reward"`, and the smoke should accept that ending as a pass while still failing a search that produced fewer than three expansions for any other reason (token ceiling, worker loss, `max_iters`/`max_calls`). Today the smoke cannot tell those apart.

## Requested code change

In `test/desktop-evolve-srbench-real.spec.ts`, step "Watch the search reach three expansions" (the block around lines 419-449): after `await save("evolve-events.json", events)`, read the `search_finished` event out of the collected events and branch before the `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(target)` assertion:

- `expanded.length >= target` — unchanged: read each candidate back by hash as the code does today.
- otherwise, if the final event is `search_finished` with `status === "succeeded"`, `stopReason === "target_reward"` and `bestTestScore >= scorecard.solvedThreshold` — record the ending (for example `metrics.stop_reason`, `metrics.expansions_planned`) and read back the candidate(s) that were actually recorded by hash, then pass.
- otherwise — keep today's failure, with a message that names `status` and `stopReason`, so a short search that ended at the budget or on an error still fails exactly as it does now (that is the #1157 case).

Please also add a regression test for the branch itself — a small unit test over the extracted predicate is enough, since the journey needs a real model — so a later edit cannot silently drop the distinction between "goal met early" and "stopped short".

## References

- Run: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405
- research-6: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135282620250
- Account for real cases: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286552958
- merge-gate: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286707014
- Report the outcome: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44415877405/job/135286834408
- Earlier green Nightly with the identical spec: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/44199315530

## Uncertainty and limits

I read the artifact's `desktop-evolve-metrics.json` and `evolve-events.json` (and the scorecard embedded in the former) plus the four failed-step logs; I did not open the Playwright trace or the journey report HTML, and I did not run the journey locally. The artifact metadata ties it to run 44415877405 and commit 59d05aa7 (its digest is the one job 135282620250 recorded), but I cannot separately prove which attempt every file inside it came from, nor which model endpoint state produced the 1.0 score. I make no claim about future Nightly runs beyond the assertion defect described.

This report does not approve development. Existing review gates and a development label applied by a person are still required.

1247.body:
### Checklist

- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] I understand that a report without environment details and a minimal reproduction is difficult to act on.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

In the desktop conversation view, while a run is active and the model is still planning ("Planning the next step"), the transcript visibly flickers. The flicker comes from an extra line appearing and disappearing just below the run line: the "Connecting to the local service…" strip.

Reproduction:

1. Open the desktop app on a session that has no pending configuration requests.
2. Send a prompt and wait until the assistant line reads "Planning the next step" (the model is thinking, before any answer or tool card).
3. Watch the transcript for several seconds.

Observed: every couple of seconds the "Connecting to the local service…" strip is inserted under the run line and then removed. The strip has padding and a bottom border, so each insertion changes the transcript height; the transcript's resize observer re-pins the scroll to the bottom, which reads as the whole conversation flashing.

Expected: the connecting strip belongs to the first read of a session's configuration data. Background re-reads during a live run must not draw it, so the transcript stays still while the model is planning.

Root cause (confirmed on the desktop source): `useConfigurationRequests` raised its `loading` state at the start of every `refresh()`. While a run is active the hook re-reads the configuration request list every two seconds (its poll) and again on every run-status or tool-status change (through the refresh key). With no configuration cards on the session, `Conversation` draws the "Connecting to the local service…" strip whenever `loading` is true and both request lists are empty, so each read blinked the strip in and out.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product: ScienceDiscovery desktop (Windows x64 build).
- Observed on: Windows; the affected code path is platform-independent and reproduces in the desktop web view on other platforms as well.
- Requires an active run and a session with no pending configuration requests; no special model or provider is needed.

### Additional Information

A fix is proposed in pull request #1244: the first read of a session scope keeps the `loading` state that draws the strip, background reads are tracked separately for poll throttling, and a refresh that reads the same list paints nothing.

### Version Information

ScienceDiscovery desktop 0.3.0, Windows x64.

1250.author: yuanzhou75
1250.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Session archive/restore already works end to end on the server and in the web client, but the desktop client has no trace of it. Because the session list defaults to `state=active`, a Session archived from the web simply **disappears** from the desktop app, with no filter to find it and no action to bring it back — the desktop cannot restore what it cannot see.

Verified on `main` `9f641cf1`:

| Where | State |
| --- | --- |
| Server routes | `POST /api/sessions/:id/archive` and `POST /api/sessions/:id/restore` exist (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:3309-3323`) |
| Server semantics | an archived Session is read-only — every write throws `Session is archived and read-only` (`services/api/src/store.ts:6385`); archiving stops the Session's notifications (`:6392`, with the comment that restore does not reopen that gate); archiving also tears down the Session's scientific-environment kernels with the reason `Session was archived; persistent memory was lost` (`http/index.ts:3315-3317`); the archive call is refused with 409 `Cannot change archive state during an active run` while a run is active (`:3311-3312`) |
| Listing | `GET /api/projects/:id/sessions` defaults to `state=active`; archived Sessions need `state=archived` or `state=all` (`http/index.ts:3147`) |
| Web client | full flow: the active/archived/all filter (`apps/web/src/session/ManagementControls.tsx:182`), both actions (`apps/web/src/api/sessions.ts:217,221`), archived labels and a read-only workspace notice |
| Desktop client | **nothing**: `apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.ts:71-78` defaults to `state="active"` and `app/use-workspace.ts:763` calls it with no state, so archived Sessions are never fetched; the Session row menu offers only 重命名 / 导出 / 删除 (`views/Sidebar.tsx:207-214`); grep for `archiv` over `apps/desktop/src` finds only research-package and file-type noise |

Impact: a desktop-only user cannot tidy a project by archiving finished Sessions at all, and a user who archived something in the web client loses access to it in the desktop app. This is the missing half of a feature the product already has.

## Design Ideas

Desktop parity, client-side only, reusing the endpoints above:

1. **Actions in the Session row menu** (`views/Sidebar.tsx`, next to 导出 / 删除): 归档 for an active Session, 恢复 for an archived one. Route through the existing `ApiClient` and refresh the project's list afterwards, so the row moves between the filters without a manual reload.
2. **A list filter in the sidebar**: 活动 / 已归档 / 全部, mapped to `state=active|archived|all` on `listSessions`. Show the archived count where the web shows it, and make 已归档 the visible home of restored-but-inactive Sessions.
3. **Say what archiving does before doing it.** The confirmation must state the two consequences the server already implements: the Session becomes read-only, and an active scientific-environment kernel is torn down (`persistent memory was lost`). Keep 删除's dialog separate — archiving is reversible, deletion is not.
4. **Archived Session page**: open it read-only — a banner in the session header, the composer disabled with the reason, and no run scheduling. Exports should keep working (they only read), so keep the export entry available; if the export path turns out to refuse an archived Session, that is worth its own issue rather than a silent disable.
5. **Handle the active-run refusal**: when a run is active, 归档/恢复 is disabled with an explanation instead of firing a 409, and if the server still answers 409 the message is shown verbatim under the row.
6. **Do not re-implement the state** — `Session.archivedAt` (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:114`) and `SessionListState` (`packages/schema/src/session.ts:69`) are already in the shared schema.

Open question to settle while implementing (not a blocker): `store.ts:6391` says restore does not reopen the notification gate that archiving closed. If a restored Session therefore cannot wake for notifications, that is a user-visible behaviour worth confirming with the owner — and if it is unintended, a separate bug rather than scope creep here.

## Involved Public APIs

No additions or changes. The desktop client consumes what exists:

- `POST /api/sessions/:id/archive`, `POST /api/sessions/:id/restore` → the updated `Session`
- `GET /api/projects/:id/sessions?state=active|archived|all`
- `Session.archivedAt` in the project payload

If a later filter or count needs a field the list does not return, that is a separate additive issue.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx` | Row-menu 归档 / 恢复; the active/archived/all filter in the list header |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts` | Fetch by state, refresh after the action, keep the selection sane when a Session leaves the current filter |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/SessionBar.tsx`, `Conversation.tsx`, `Composer.tsx` | Archived read-only banner and a disabled composer |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/{zh,en}.ts`, styles | Copy, confirmation, disabled reasons |
| `apps/web` | Reference implementation; unchanged |
| `services/api`, `packages/*` | Untouched |

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Component tests**: the filter requests `state=archived|all` and renders those Sessions; 归档 calls `POST …/archive` and the row leaves 活动 on refresh; 恢复 calls `POST …/restore` and the row returns; an active run disables the action with a reason and a 409 surfaces the server text; an archived Session renders the read-only banner with the composer disabled; zh-CN and en copy both covered.
- **E2E on the desktop build with the real stack**: archive a Session → it leaves 活动 and appears under 已归档; open it (read-only, composer disabled, export still reachable); restore it → back under 活动 and writable; try to archive while a run is active → refused with the explanation; archive a Session whose scientific environment has a live kernel → the confirmation mentions the memory loss and the kernel is torn down.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots (active list, archived filter with a restored row, archive confirmation, archived read-only Session, active-run refusal) go in the PR body for the owner's approval.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The desktop sidebar filters Sessions by 活动 / 已归档 / 全部, and the choice survives a reload.
- [ ] An active Session can be archived from its row menu; it leaves 活动 and appears under 已归档 without a manual refresh.
- [ ] An archived Session can be restored from the same menu and becomes writable again.
- [ ] Archiving asks for confirmation that names the read-only state and the scientific-kernel teardown; deletion keeps its own separate dialog.
- [ ] An archived Session opens read-only with a visible banner and a composer that says why it cannot send.
- [ ] With a run active, 归档/恢复 is disabled with the reason, and a 409 from the server is shown rather than swallowed.
- [ ] No server, schema or packaging change is in the diff; both locales covered.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body.

## Additional Information

Verified by reading `main` `9f641cf1` before filing: the two routes and their guards (`http/index.ts:3309-3323`), the store's read-only rule and notification stop (`store.ts:6385-6410`), the list default (`http/index.ts:3147`), the web implementation, and the desktop client's `state="active"` default with no archive surface.

The web client is the behavioural reference for copy and flow; the desktop should match its semantics rather than invent new ones, including the "reversible" framing of archive versus delete.

1251.author: yuanzhou75
1251.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The desktop client has no way to find a Session except scrolling the sidebar. The server already serves a workbench search and the web client already consumes it, so this is a client gap rather than a new capability.

Verified on `main` `9f641cf1`:

| Piece | State |
| --- | --- |
| Search endpoint | `GET /api/search?q=&limit=&offset=` (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:1818-1824`) → `searchWorkbench` (`services/api/src/workbench/index.ts:29-93`) |
| What it matches | project **names**; Session **titles** (plus project name and Session id); artifact **names/titles** (plus their Session title and project). It does **not** look inside messages |
| Result shape | `WorkbenchSearchResult` with `kind: "project" \| "session" \| "artifact"`, project/session context, `archived` flag for Sessions, and `hasMore`/`total` paging |
| Web client | a palette in the composer (`apps/web/src/composer/WorkbenchNavigation.tsx:103` debounce, `:164` client-side filtering, `@`/`#` triggers) |
| Desktop client | **nothing**: no `/api/search` call anywhere in `apps/desktop/src`, no search field, no result list |

Two secondary gaps in the desktop list itself:

- The sidebar only ever asks for `state="active"` (`apps/desktop/src/api/sessions.ts:71-78` and its only caller `app/use-workspace.ts:763`), so nothing but the default view exists. The archive-state filter is tracked in `#1250`; this issue should not duplicate it.
- There is no filter other than "which project am I in": no by-kind, no by-time, no "has artifacts / is running".

Message-content search is a real user need, but `searchWorkbench` only reads titles today; adding it means an index and belongs to a follow-up once this UI exists.

## Design Ideas

1. **A search field at the top of the session sidebar** (and the same one reachable from the command palette if the desktop gains one): debounce ~250 ms like the web client, call `GET /api/search`, and render results grouped by kind — 项目 / 会话 / 产物 — with the project context and an `已归档` marker on archived Sessions.
2. **Keyboard first**: `Ctrl/Cmd+K` opens it, arrow keys move, `Enter` opens the result (Session → open, project → switch, artifact → open its dialog). Escape closes and restores the previous list.
3. **Filters for the session list**, applied client-side over the returned page while the result set is small: 仅当前项目 / 全部项目, 仅运行中, 有产物的会话, and a time window (今天 / 最近 7 天 / 全部). State (活动/已归档/全部) stays with `#1250`.
4. **Be honest about the search scope**: label the field so it does not promise message search ("搜索会话、项目、产物"), and put the content-search follow-up in the issue rather than faking it.
5. **Empty and error states**: a query with no results says so with the current scope; an API failure shows the reason and a retry instead of an empty list.

If the client-side filters prove insufficient, `GET /api/search` can gain additive `kind`/`projectId` params later; this issue should work without them.

## Involved Public APIs

Consumed only, no changes required:

- `GET /api/search?q=&limit=&offset=` → `WorkbenchSearchResponse` (`results[]`, `total`, `hasMore`)
- `GET /api/projects/:id/sessions?state=…` for the list itself

If scoped search parameters are added later, that is a separate additive change.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/api/workbench.ts` (new) | `search(q, limit, offset)` client |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/Sidebar.tsx` | Search field, result list, filter row |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/use-workspace.ts` | Query state, selection after a result opens, refresh behaviour |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/{zh,en}.ts`, styles | Copy and layout |
| `apps/web` | Reference only (its palette is the behavioural model) |
| `services/api`, `packages/*` | Untouched |

Related, non-overlapping: `#1250` (archive/restore filter and actions).

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Component tests**: typing debounces and issues one request per settled query; results render grouped by kind with project context and the archived marker; keyboard navigation opens the right target; filters narrow the session list and persist for the session; empty result and API failure states.
- **E2E on the desktop build with the real stack**: search a term that only a Session title contains, one that only an artifact name contains, and one that only a message body contains (the last must return nothing and say why); open a result with the keyboard; filter to 仅运行中 during a run and back.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots (empty field, results grouped by kind, filters applied, no-result state) go in the PR body for the owner's approval.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A search field in the desktop sidebar queries `/api/search` with debounce and renders results grouped by 项目 / 会话 / 产物 with their context.
- [ ] Archived Sessions in the results carry an 已归档 marker, and opening one lands in the read-only view.
- [ ] `Ctrl/Cmd+K` focuses search, arrows move the selection, `Enter` opens it, Escape closes.
- [ ] The session list can be narrowed by 仅当前项目 / 仅运行中 / 有产物 / 时间窗口, and the choice survives a reload.
- [ ] No results and API failures are distinguishable, and both offer the next step.
- [ ] The field's copy does not imply message-content search; that gap is recorded as a follow-up in the issue.
- [ ] zh-CN and en copy; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body.

## Additional Information

Verified on `main` `9f641cf1`: the endpoint and its matcher (`workbench/index.ts:39-83` — names/titles only, no message bodies), the web palette's debounce and client-side kinds, and the absence of any search client or UI in `apps/desktop/src`.

Out of scope here: message-content search (needs an index; follow-up), the archive-state filter (`#1250`), and any change to what `searchWorkbench` indexes.
